description: Focused long-context suite covering two domains where task identity stays stable while local deltas accumulate across many turns.
notes: Use this suite for faster iteration before running the full long-context benchmark.
These two cases should expose whether token savings grow as session history accumulates.

cases.goal: Write and iteratively reshape a product article while the audience, tone, evidence, and publishing constraints drift over time.
turns: You are drafting a 600-word article about a new internal analytics dashboard for engineering managers. Start by giving a concise outline with headline, 3 section headers, and one-sentence takeaway.
Keep the same article, but change the target audience to startup CTOs instead of engineering managers. Update only what must change in the outline.
New constraint: avoid hype and avoid the words revolutionary, game-changing, and seamless. Revise the outline accordingly.
Add this new evidence to the story: the dashboard cut weekly manual reporting time from 6 hours to 90 minutes in a pilot team. Update the outline and the main claim.
The user now wants the piece to mention one adoption risk: missing data definitions across teams. Fold that in without changing the overall structure more than necessary.
Actually shorten the article target from 600 words to 350 words and make it suitable for a newsletter. Provide the revised outline only.
New issue: legal asks that you avoid promising ROI. Update the framing while keeping the rest intact.
Finish by outputting a final short article draft in 5 tight paragraphs.

cases.goal: Develop an OpenClaw agent feature through multiple code, prompt, and behavior corrections across a longer debugging session.
turns: Design a small plan for adding a retry wrapper around a flaky tool call in an OpenClaw agent. Keep it to 4 bullets.
New constraint: retries must not duplicate side effects. Update only the plan items that change.
Add this implementation detail: the tool sometimes times out after 15 seconds but succeeds on the second call. Revise the plan.
The user now wants jittered backoff and a max of 3 attempts. Update the relevant bullets.
New problem: logs show the wrapper hides the original error cause. Adjust the design to preserve debuggability.
Actually the wrapper should not retry validation errors at all. Refine the retry policy.
Add a requirement that the agent summary must state whether the final success came from the first try or a retry.
New issue: a reviewer points out the wrapper might trap cancellation signals. Correct the design.
The user changes the goal slightly: the first delivery can be pseudocode and test strategy instead of final code. Adapt the output expectation.
Final turn: provide the final pseudocode plus 5 focused test cases.
